newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE-Recovery amid healthy demand, firm U.S.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE-Recovery amid healthy demand, firm U.S.

text.p: Asian MTBE weekly prices staged a recovery amid healthy demand and sharp gains in Europe and the U.S., but the weak gasoline market is keeping a lid on the gasoline octane booster's recovery, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"It is very strong now," a producer said. "Everyone is looking for cargoes...blenders, traders and endusers."
Singapore free-on-board (fob) MTBE parcels lifting in July were heard traded in a range of $260-$265 per tonne with sellers indicating "$260 at the least".
Last week, prices were assessed lower at $255/$260.
"There had been a fair bit of demand," a trader said. "All of a sudden, demand from blenders has picked up."
Both traders and producers said around three to four blenders were looking for July parcels, mainly on the back of high-octane gasoline demand into Indonesia and Taiwan.
They also said enduser demand was heard from refiner Thai Oil which was seeking 3,500 tonnes for delivery in July while it is negotiating its second half-year term supplies for around 63,000-tonnes.
Sources said they expected the term contract to be concluded sometime next week.
Asian prices have also edged up with stronger worlwide prices, they said.
"With the other markets galloping away, this market is trying to narrow the difference but it is still miles away," said a producer.
He said prices in Europe and the U.S. Gulf were around $40 per tonne higher at around $300 per tonne.
Traders in the U.S. said prices had risen sharply amid blending demand and continued tight supplies until August with plant turnarounds.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) last week awarded its buy tender for August at the same level as its July award.
It bought two 3,500-tonne cargoes for August 6-20 delivery from two producers at $270 per tonne, cost-and-freight to Kaohsiung or Keelung.
"Gasoline is keeping a lid on the MTBE," a producer said.
Gasoline prices in Singapore extended its losses amid weak regional demand.
Benchmark 95-octane gasoline fell by another 40 cents per barrel to $23.45 from the same point last week.
"It is a good time for (MTBE) sellers," a trader said. "But it is not a big jump and who knows how long demand will last."
